jobs.company: Metropolitan Water District of Southern California
jobs.title: Senior Environmental Specialist
jobs.description:
At the Metropolitan Water District of Southern California, we deliver reliable water to a region with 19 million people—and to accomplish this, we rely on a team of talented employees: innovators, problem-solvers, and collaborators who make it all possible.

There is currently one (1) opening for Senior Environmental Specialist located at Union Station, Los Angeles, CA.

This recruitment may result in an eligibility list*.

Job Summary

The Senior Environmental Specialist leads the development, coordination, and implementation of complex environmental, health, and safety (EHS) compliance programs and technical studies across multiple Metropolitan sites. Serving as a technical subject matter expert, this role provides high-level program management and regulatory oversight across key disciplines including air quality, wastewater, stormwater, underground and aboveground storage tanks, hazardous materials and waste management, and health and safety. Based at the Los Angeles Headquarters, this position requires periodic travel and occasional overnight stays at field facilities throughout Southern California.

What You’ll Do

Program & Compliance Leadership: Formulate compliance strategies, secure environmental permits, and review changing legislation to assess organizational impacts. Monitor federal, state, and local regulations to minimize risk for employees, the environment, and the public.
Technical Systems & Data Tracking: Utilize specialized Environmental Management Information System (EMIS) software and online platforms—including, but not limited to: SCAQMD Permit Database, CARB DOORS/R3 databases, CERS, GeoTracker, LACPW EPIC system, CalOES Spill Reporting, and the DTSC Hazardous WasteTracking System—to manage compliance data and streamline cloud-based tracking tools.
Agency Collaboration & Liaison: Serve as a primary point of contact for regulatory agencies, local governments, and member agencies. Lead negotiations, respond to inquiries, and establish strong partnerships with internal and external entities to represent Metropolitan's operational interests.
Internal Partnership & Training: Partner with internal teams to evaluate day-to-day compliance, deliver technical expertise, make recommendations to supervisors, and design EHS awareness and training programs for personnel.
Reporting & Documentation: Conduct staff analyses, execute complex environmental studies, and prepare technical reports, general correspondence, and Board letters for management review.

Schedule:
9/80, Monday through Friday with every other Friday off

This job announcement has been designed to indicate the general nature and level of work being performed by employees in this classification / job.

To view the full job description click here: Sr. Environmental Specialist

Schedule: 9/80
Start times are no earlier than 6 am and end times are no later than 6 pm.

Hybrid:
Metropolitan’s current practice in this position is a hybrid work schedule. This typically includes two days a week in person and the other days remote. This is subject to change dependent on organizational needs. In addition, a telework policy is scheduled for negotiations and once completed and implemented, will provide final direction on the hybrid schedule.

EMPLOYMENT STANDARDS

Minimum Qualifications

Education and Experience:
Bachelor’s degree from an accredited college or university in environmental science, engineering, biology, ecology, planning, or other directly related field, and eight years of progressively responsible experience, including two years at the Environmental Specialist level or equivalent; or a master’s degree from an accredited college or university in environmental science, engineering, biology, ecology, planning, or other directly related field, and six years of progressively responsible experience including two years at the Environmental Specialist level or equivalent.

Relevant/Related Experience is defined as:
demonstrated experience serving as a lead for Environmental, Health, and Safety (EHS) programs, including managing multi-media environmental compliance areas such as Air Quality and Permitting, Underground Storage Tanks (UST), Industrial Wastewater, NPDES stormwater/wastewater reporting, and Hazardous Material Management.

Desirable Qualifications:

Environmental, Health, and Safety, Water Quality - Experience in public sector, water industry, public utilities; Certified Hazardous Materials Manager (CHMM); Certified Safety Professional (CSP); SCAQMD Certified Permitting Professional (CPP).

Certifications, Licenses, And Registration Requirements

License(s): Valid California Class C Driver’s License or equivalent (required at time of application) that allows you to drive during your employment.

CLOSING

Benefits

Competitive compensation
Excellent medical, dental, life, vision plans.
Deferred compensation in the form of a 401(k) plan (with matching contribution) and a 457 plan.
Retirement benefits under the California Public Employees' Retirement System
Tuition reimbursement
Training and advancement opportunities
Excellent working environment
Public transportation reimbursements
Hub of public transportation: rail, subway, buses, and taxis
On-site fitness center

For more information on MWD benefits, please use the following link: Benefits Regular Full Time Employee (Represented)

About Mwd

The Metropolitan Water District of Southern California is a state-established cooperative that, along with its 26 cities and retail suppliers, provides water for 19 million people in six counties. The district imports water from the Colorado River and Northern California to supplement local supplies, and helps its members to develop increased water conservation, recycling, storage and other resource-management programs.

The Metropolitan Water District of Southern California is committed to providing reasonable accommodations to qualified individuals with disabilities. Qualified individuals with disabilities, who need a reasonable accommodation during the application or selection process, please call (213) 217-7738 or email: jobs@mwdh2o.com.

Metropolitan is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to disability, status as a protected veteran, or any other protected characteristic(s).

Application Filing Period:
Closes at 4:30 pm PT on the date stated in the job announcement. However it may close prior to the filing end date if sufficient applications have been received. If sufficient applications have not been received, then the filing period end date may be extended.

Eligibility List*:
An eligibility list is a list of qualified candidates created when a job posting states that one will be established.

Candidates who meet the minimum qualifications listed in the original posting and successfully pass all stages of the recruitment process—but are not selected for the initial vacancy—may be placed on this list for future openings.

The list may be used to invite candidates to participate in a selection interview for a future vacancy in the same classification / title (if there is one). The duration of the list depends on the applicable bargaining unit.

Qualifying Experience:
Your resume must at a minimum include the month and year you began and ended employment, name of the organization, your title, and a brief description of your experience. If your employment was part-time, make sure you identify it on your resume next to the month/year.

Sponsorship:
Applicants for employment with The Metropolitan Water District of Southern California must have work authorization that does not now or in the future require sponsorship of a visa for employment authorization in the United States (i.e., H1-B or other employment-based immigration case).

jobs.title: Environmental Health Safety Specialist
jobs.description:
Title:
Environmental, Health & Safety (EHS) Specialist
Location
: Universal City, CA
Pay Rate
: $40/hour
Duration
: Contract through February 2027

Position Summary

The Environmental, Health & Safety (EHS) Specialist will support environmental compliance and safety initiatives across Studio and Theme Park operations. This role will conduct inspections, monitor environmental programs, identify compliance gaps, coordinate with internal departments and regulatory agencies, and support corrective actions. The ideal candidate will have strong knowledge of environmental regulations, excellent communication skills, and the ability to achieve results through influence and cross-functional collaboration
.

Job Responsibilities

Work with various departments within Studio and Theme Park to assess compliance with environmental requirements.
Conduct inspections of storage tank locations listed in the Spill Prevention Control and Countermeasure Plan (SPCC)
.
Identify items needing correction or attention and work with relevant teams on resolution.
Identify tanks not listed in the SPCC Plan or altered and draft amendments.
Conduct inspections of hazardous materials storage locations.
Confirm that inventory listed in CERS
is consistent with observations and make necessary changes.
Conduct general housekeeping inspections of material handling areas, including hazmat and food areas.
Recommend improvements to Best Management Practices (BMPs)
and work with identified groups to improve housekeeping.
Inspect stormwater treatment and capture devices throughout the property.
Conduct daily drives of River Road to confirm diversions are operating properly.
Gather stormwater flow data from diversion totalizers and input data into spreadsheets, identifying trend changes.
Coordinate and accompany agency inspectors from County and City CUPA.
Gather monthly hazardous waste manifests and prepare an itemized spreadsheet for tracking and cost allocation.
Assist with Asbestos Written Determinations.
Perform other safety and health-related work as requested.

Basic Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in EHS, Engineering, Chemistry, or Biology
.
1–3 years of EHS experience
.
Experience with EHS technical programs.
Comfortable working in an environment where direction occurs through influence
.
Computer savvy and comfortable working with enterprise software.
Excellent professional verbal and written communication skills.

Show more

Show less

Seniority level

Associate

Employment type

Contract

Job function

Quality Assurance

Industries

Staffing and Recruiting
